subject: maths
question: A can complete a piece of work in 24 days and B can complete it in 28 days. If they work on alternate days, starting with B on the first day, then in how many days will the work be finished?
solution:
**Given:**

A can complete work in 24 days

B can complete work in 28 days

They work on alternate days starting with B

**Formula used:**

LCM method: Assume total work = LCM of 24 and 28

Work per day = Total work ÷ Time

Alternate day work: Add work done by B and A alternately

**Calculation:**

⇒ LCM of 24 and 28 = 168 units (assume total work)

⇒ A's 1 day work = 168 ÷ 24 = 7 units

⇒ B's 1 day work = 168 ÷ 28 = 6 units

⇒ Work in 2 days (B + A) = 6 + 7 = 13 units

Now, total work = 168 units

⇒ 13 units done every 2 days

⇒ Work done in 12 full cycles (24 days) = 12 × 13 = 156 units

⇒ Remaining work = 168 − 156 = 12 units

⇒ Next day is B’s turn (since last was A)

⇒ B does 6 units on 25th day, remaining = 12 − 6 = 6 units

⇒ A does 7 units per day, but only 6 units needed

⇒ A will finish in 6 ÷ 7 = 6/7 day

⇒ Total days = 25 + 6/7 = 25⁶⁄₇ days

**∴ The work will be finished in 25⁶⁄₇ days**
